scope: Ratio-disagreement pixel parity: the accepted SPK-13 probe documents are driven read-only, but the browser context deviceScaleFactor and the dpr the page is asked to render at deliberately differ per row. Reference still adopts the target native float32 camera/viewport/scissor, so the claim stays the splat rasterisation/sort/blend path.
strictRule: RGBA read-back compared by sha256 over the raw bytes (equal hashes = every channel byte difference is 0, no tolerance); drawing buffer must follow the REQUESTED ratio not the device ratio; both images non-empty; each side stable against its own repeat; identical splat counts; identical context attributes, unmasked renderer and observed devicePixelRatio across the two documents; zero JS and drained GL errors; negative control must move pixels; the accepted pixel gate probe/bundle fingerprints must be unchanged and the source digest must not move during the run.
claimLimit: Per-engine evidence on THIS machine only. Where a browser clamps the requested device ratio to the ratio the page was asked for, the row records mismatchProven=false and does not count as exercising the disagreement - see counts.rowsWithMismatchProven. Nothing here generalises to other GPUs, drivers or devices, and it is not a release READY claim.
methodDifference: Single loopback origin instead of the pixel gate two-origin layout (that gate owns the cross-origin anti-cheat). Here isolation is asserted from the request sets: the target document must never request a /dist/ reference asset and the reference must never request the SDK build.
